findings.locator: Published pp857-859 Theorem1.1,Corollary1.2,definitions and proof outline; main theorem proof not read
findings.input: G(n,p) with independent edges,p=omega(loglog(n)/n); high probability as n tends to infinity.
findings.output: Edge partition into odd(G)/2+np/2+o(n) cycles and single edges. The n/4+np/2+o(n) corollary also needs p<1-omega(1/n).
findings.scope: Odd-degree lower bound and cycle-size bound motivate the count. Euler means all degrees even, connectivity not required; log is natural. Outline separates sparse/intermediate/dense ranges.
findings.cannot_transfer: No deterministic arbitrary finite graph guarantee,effective n0,or implementation runtime. Do not replace odd(G)/2 by n/4 arbitrarily near p=1.

findings.locator: arXivv2 pp1-4 definitions,Theorems1.3/1.5/1.7 and selected1.3 proof; pp9-10 Theorem5.1 and selected1.7 proof
findings.input: Finite simple graphs; source use of1.3 has positive order n and maximum degree<=4;1.7 source uses graphs containing a cycle.
findings.output: Theorem1.3 f_ce<=n-1 for maxdegree<=4; Theorem1.7 g_ce<=n-2 for a graph that is not a tree. f_ce partitions cycles/edges; g_ce covers and may repeat edges.
findings.scope: Non-tree includes disconnected forests with at least two components. Here Eulerian means connected and even. Theorem1.5 counts 2-regular parts, each may have many cycle components. Selected1.3 and1.7 proofs read, not accepted or fully recursively audited.
